note: Contract with Unreal v0: what Unreal has wired, so the editor can warn before an edit breaks the experience. Built by hand from the tools audit (docs/editor-obra/anexos/11 and 17). The harvest (F3) will verify and refresh each entry. Severity per action: block | warn | info.
verified: 2026-10-01 (from files and dumps; live verification pending)

entries.msg: Stage title times are literals in BP_Obra_SC › RunObra (in 0.5→1.8 s, out 4.6→5.6 s). The APK keeps them until the graph changes.
Veil times are literals in BP_Obra_SC › FlowVeil (opens 1→4 s, closes 69→71.5 s). The APK keeps them until the graph changes.
Which ambience plays when is decided in BP_Obra_SC › AmbPick (literal indices). The APK keeps its own choice.
This voice is called by an Unreal graph (by asset path, or by array index in the Hall). Its timing there is decided by AlmaSpeak, StageCues, StepStageVO or HallSay.
entries.msgDelete: Deleting the voice here won't silence it in the APK: the graph still calls it.

entries.msg: The bell timeout is the knob FW_Bell (25 s, final value) in HallDirector. After it, the bell fills by itself in 3 s.
The sensor timeout is the knob FW_Tool (20 s, final value) in HallDirector.
The soul-choice timeout is the knob FW_Choose (25 s, final value) in HallDirector.
The share timeout is the knob ShareFW (30 s). The default answer at timeout is wired to bSimulated (literal).
In Unreal this is not a blocking wait: the stage runs on its clock. The user's gesture only decides if the help voice plays (HelpAfter).
In Unreal this is a non-blocking condition (CueAttract / CueDraw thresholds), not a wait.
Stage timeouts are literals in BP_Obra_SC › RunObra (180 / 120 / 240 s) and call CallOutro without SAVE or coda.
Haptic patterns don't exist in Unreal yet (only HapticAmp 0.25 while breathing and the bell). This element is preview only.
